subject: Computing

source.title: National curriculum in England: computing programmes of study

statementPolicy: Controlled paraphrases of the statutory programme of study, not verbatim curriculum text. Example content shown in square brackets in the source is not treated as a statutory objective.

KS2: Sequence, selection, repetition, variables, input and output
Search and evaluation of digital content

KS1.summary: Understand algorithms as precise instructions and recognise how algorithms are implemented as programs on digital devices.
Create simple programs and debug them when they do not behave as intended.
Use logical reasoning to predict the behaviour of simple programs.
Use technology purposefully to create, organise, store, manipulate and retrieve digital content.
Recognise common uses of information technology beyond school.
Use technology safely and respectfully, protect personal information, and know where to seek help about concerning online content or contact.

KS2.summary: Design, write and debug programs for specific goals, including controlling or simulating physical systems, and decompose problems into smaller parts.

KS2.domain: Sequence, selection, repetition, variables, input and output
KS2.summary: Use sequence, selection and repetition in programs and work with variables plus different forms of input and output.
Use logical reasoning to explain simple algorithms and identify and correct errors in algorithms and programs.
Understand computer networks, including the internet, their services such as the World Wide Web, and opportunities for communication and collaboration.

KS2.domain: Search and evaluation of digital content
KS2.summary: Use search technologies effectively, understand that results are selected and ranked, and evaluate digital content critically.
Select and combine software and internet services across digital devices to create programs, systems and content, including collecting, analysing, evaluating and presenting data and information.
Use technology safely, respectfully and responsibly, recognise acceptable and unacceptable behaviour, and know ways to report concerns about content or contact.

KS3.summary: Design, use and evaluate computational abstractions that model the state and behaviour of real-world problems and physical systems.
Understand key algorithms associated with computational thinking and use logical reasoning to compare the usefulness of alternative algorithms.
Use at least two programming languages, including one textual language, to solve computational problems and use suitable data structures, procedures and functions.
Understand Boolean logic and some applications in circuits and programming, and represent and operate on numbers in binary.
Understand the hardware and software components of computer systems and how systems communicate with each other.
Understand how instructions are stored and executed and how text, sound and pictures can be represented and manipulated digitally using binary digits.
Create projects using multiple applications and devices to collect and analyse data and meet the needs of known users.
Create, reuse, revise and repurpose digital artefacts for a defined audience, considering trustworthiness, design and usability.
Use technology safely, respectfully, responsibly and securely, including protecting online identity and privacy and reporting inappropriate content, contact or conduct.

KS4.summary: Develop capability, creativity and knowledge in computer science at sufficient depth to support progression to higher study or professional careers.
Develop capability, creativity and knowledge in digital media and apply them to practical and analytical tasks.
Develop capability, creativity and knowledge in information technology and apply them to practical and analytical tasks.
Develop and apply analytical, problem-solving, design and computational thinking skills.
Understand how technological change affects safety, including new approaches to protecting online privacy and identity and reporting concerns.
